subject: ventures/gtin-list-check
professional: a GS1 data / retail catalogue specialist who cleans supplier item files before marketplace or retailer upload; they check first that the mod-10 check digit is computed per GS1 General Specifications for GTIN-8/12/13/14, that GTINs are compared in 14-digit form, that prefix rules (RCN 02/04/2x, coupons 05/99/981-984, refund 980, ISBN 978/979, ISSN 977, RCN-8 GS1-8 prefixes 0/2) are applied to the right digits for each GTIN length, that UPC-E is expanded correctly, and that nothing mangled by Excel is 'repaired' into a code the data cannot prove

evidence.correctness: Independent GS1 mod-10 written by the auditor from GS1 General Specifications section 7.9.1 (weights 3,1,3... from the rightmost body digit, check = round-up-to-ten minus sum) in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/cb322ece-d3bb-5c74-9693-c3fe9f6815e5/scratchpad/gtin/probe.mjs, run with node. The core is right: 0 disagreements with computeCheck over 200,000 random 7/11/12/13-digit bodies; published codes 5449000000996 (Coca-Cola 330 ml), 3017620422003 (Nutella 400 g), 4006381333931, 036000291452, 9780306406157, 96385074, 73513537, 9771473968012, 5000159484695 all validate; hand-worked body 400638133393 -> 1 matches; ISBN-10 080442957X -> 9780804429573 matches; UPC-E pattern g=4 (01234543 -> 012340000053) matches the GS1 zero-suppression table; 4 spellings of one UPC (12, 11, 13, 14 digits, apostrophe) give 4 duplicate warnings. Wrong outputs a user would act on: (1) Excel scientific notation with rounded-away digits is 'expanded' and written into the repaired file whenever the zero-filled value happens to pass mod-10 (1 in 10): classify('1.0009E+11') -> ok 100090000000 'the check digit confirms it', and repair() writes 100090000000 into the file. Digits that were rounded away cannot be confirmed by a check digit. (2) Every 14-digit GTIN whose second digit is 2, 4 or 5 after a 0 indicator is flagged as a GS1 restricted prefix: 04006381333931 (Stabilo, GTIN-14 form) -> 'Restricted prefix 04', 05000159484695 (UK EAN-13 in GTIN-14 form) -> 'Restricted prefix 05 (coupons)', and an indicator-2 case code 20036000291456 -> 'Restricted prefix 2'; meanwhile a case code wrapping a real RCN is missed. The prefix regexes run on padStart(13), which does nothing to a 14-digit value. (3) An 8-digit UPC-E whose digits also pass GTIN-8 mod-10 (about 1 in 10) is kept silently as a GTIN-8 with GS1-8 prefix 0 (an RCN-8), not expanded: the tool's own UPC-E fixture 01234565 (UPC-A 012345000065 per its own test) classifies as GTIN-8 01234565, and listing both forms gives no duplicate warning. Correctness capped at 2 by these three wrong outputs despite an exact core.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked by running calc.mjs: check-digit errors with adjacent-swap hint (works, 4006381333913 -> suggests 4006381333931); leading zeros restored (works, also for 9- and 10-digit inputs the page does not mention); scientific notation expanded / flagged (works except the coincidence case above); duplicates across UPC/EAN-13 forms (works); blanks, placeholders (works, 000000000000 error); reserved prefixes (works for 12/13-digit, wrong for 14-digit); ISBN-10 -> 13 (works); UPC-E expansion (works when it is not also a valid GTIN-8); GTIN-14 case-pack linking (works); Digital Link, (01), ]E0 unwrapping (tests pass); write-back with optional fixed length and Excel-safe wrapper (works); UTF-16 decode (works). Served page https://marisstella.app/gtin-list-check/ returns 200 and served llms.txt points at marisstella.app. No stubs or TODOs. README's test command fails on Node 22.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' from ventures/gtin-list-check: 37 pass, 0 fail, 0.3 s. Mutations (each reverted with git checkout, git status clean at the end): weights 3,1 -> 1,3 at calc.mjs:17 caught (17 fail); skipping the 04 restricted prefix at calc.mjs:152 survived; UPC-E g=4 expansion changed to the g=3 layout at calc.mjs:38 survived (the 'every suppression pattern' test at calc.test.mjs:134 has no g=4 case); sci-notation 'lost > 0' -> 'lost > 1' at calc.mjs:105 survived; duplicate key padStart(14) -> padStart(12) at calc.mjs:204 caught; case-pack inner check computed on the wrong slice at calc.mjs:225 caught. 3 of 6 survived. A seventh (removing the length break at calc.mjs:132) is an equivalent mutant (zero padding preserves validity) and is not counted. No test covers a GTIN-14 with a prefix check, or a sci value whose zero fill passes mod-10.

Disclaimer, independence note, 'read from memory of public GS1 specifications' present (index.html footer, line 115) - pass. 'GS1 reserved prefixes (02, 04, 05, 2xx, 981-985, 99)' (index.html:114) - partial: wrong on GTIN-14, omits 980 refund receipts and RCN-8 prefixes. evidence.fitness: Walked the first-visitor job (seller with an 'invalid GTIN' rejection): pasted sampleBrokenFile and a mixed list; the tool names each bad line, fixes lost zeros and ISBN-10s, and downloads a repaired CSV. For UPC/EAN-13 lists that works. A catalogue specialist hits problems in the first hour: GTIN-14 exports (common from PIMs and GDSN) raise false 'restricted prefix' warnings on ordinary German and UK items, about 1 in 10 UPC-Es is left as a restricted GTIN-8, and the 'fixed' file can contain a fabricated GTIN from a scientific-notation cell, which is exactly the error the tool is meant to stop. European Excel output with a decimal comma ('4,006381333931E+12' in a ';' file) is reported as 'non-digit characters', not as scientific notation.
evidence.domain: Compared with GS1 General Specifications: mod-10 (7.9.1), GTIN-14 indicator semantics and inner-GTIN derivation, UPC-E zero-suppression table and ISBN-10 to Bookland 978 conversion are right. Departures: prefix rules are applied to a 13-digit pad of the value rather than to the GS1 prefix position of each GTIN format (for GTIN-14, positions 2 onward), so indicator digits are read as prefixes; RCN-8 (GS1-8 prefixes 0 and 2) and the 980 refund-receipt range are not flagged (9800000000007 and 20123451 produce no finding); an 8-digit string that is valid both as GTIN-8 and as UPC-E is not reported as ambiguous although a 0-prefixed GTIN-8 is an RCN-8 and the UPC-E reading is the likely one in North American data; check-digit agreement is presented as proof for recovered digits, which no GS1 practitioner would accept for rounded scientific-notation values.

defects.what: Scientific-notation cells with rounded-away digits are accepted as valid whenever the zero-filled value passes mod-10 (about 1 in 10), reported as 'the check digit confirms it' and written into the repaired file: 1.0009E+11 -> 100090000000. Lost digits cannot be confirmed; any lost > 0 should be sci-lost.

Restricted-prefix rules run on c.value.padStart(13), a no-op for GTIN-14, so the indicator digit is read as the prefix: 04006381333931 flagged 'in-store', 05000159484695 flagged 'coupons', indicator-2 case codes flagged 'in-store'; RCNs wrapped in a non-zero indicator are missed.

An 8-digit code valid both as GTIN-8 and as UPC-E (about 1 in 10 UPC-Es, including the test fixture 01234565) is kept as a GS1-8-prefix-0 GTIN-8 (an RCN-8) with no ambiguity warning, and a duplicate with its UPC-A form goes undetected.
Tests do not cover a GTIN-14 prefix check, the 04 rule, the UPC-E g=4 pattern (despite the test title 'every suppression pattern'), or the sci coincidence case; 3 of 6 seeded mutations survived.
Prefix list omits 980 (refund receipts) and RCN-8 GS1-8 prefixes 0 and 2: 9800000000007 and 20123451 pass without a finding.
Decimal-comma scientific notation from European Excel ('4,006381333931E+12') is reported as 'non-digit characters' instead of being expanded or flagged.
README and page say lost zeros are 'proven' / restored for 7, 11 or 13 digits; mod-10 rejects only 9 in 10 wrong candidates and 9- and 10-digit inputs are also padded.
repair() drops all-empty rows and rewrites line endings while documenting that rows it cannot fix are left exactly as they were.
README test command 'node --test ventures/gtin-list-check/' fails on Node 22 (Cannot find module); use node --test 'ventures/gtin-list-check/*.test.mjs'.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2; median 2); finished (completeness 3). The GS1 mod-10 core is exact (0 disagreements in 200,000 random bodies against an independent implementation; nine published GTINs, ISBN-10 with X and the UPC-E table all match), and the tool does everything it lists for ordinary UPC/EAN-13 lists. A GS1 data specialist would not sign it off: a scientific-notation cell whose digits were rounded away is 'confirmed' and written back as a fabricated GTIN about 1 time in 10 (1.0009E+11 -> 100090000000), every 0-indicator GTIN-14 of a German or UK EAN-13 is flagged as a restricted/coupon prefix because the prefix check reads the indicator digit, and about 1 in 10 UPC-Es is kept silently as an RCN-8 GTIN-8. Three of six seeded mutations in core logic (04 prefix, UPC-E g=4, sci guard) left all 37 tests green.
